title: Relational Time Flow from Particles’ Internal Cyclic Times: Why Elementary Cycles Theory Works
content: Elementary particles exhibit intrinsic phase recurrences, implicit in their undulatory description, so that each can serve, in principle, as an ultra-precise relativistic reference clock, with ticking rate universally fixed by the particle’s mass through the Compton relation. From this perspective, Rovelli’s “timeless” viewpoint is best read not as denying time, but as denying the fundamentality of any preferred external time coordinate. The physically relevant temporal variables are identified here with the particles’ intrinsic cyclic times, covariantly modulated by energy exchange and relativistic transformations, whereas the ordinary external time axis is reconstructed operationally through cycle counting and records. The present work is therefore not merely a reinterpretation of relational time, but addresses a specific consistency problem: how compact microscopic temporal variables, fixed by de Broglie–Compton periodicity, can yield the ordinary non-compact relativistic time flow observed in nature. Macroscopic time flow and its effective irreversibility then arise through coarse graining and the accumulation of records, allowing a relational-clock reformulation of the usual tension between Hamiltonian time reversal and the second law of thermodynamics, including the Loschmidt-paradox viewpoint. The proposal involves no adjustable fine-tuning, no hidden Planck-scale assumptions, and no arbitrary choice of clock variables. The internal consistency of describing time flow in terms of internal cyclic times is established here, while its connection with covariant modulations, interactions, and exact quantization has been developed in previous work on Elementary Cycles Theory.
